A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same federated Granger causality framework and contain 29 pages, including Appendices A.1–A.9. Text comparison and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables and appendices.

before.justification: Sections 8–9 report original synthetic-system and HAI/SWaT experiments, including causality estimates, robustness tests, scalability results and communication savings.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experimental results in Sections 8–9, Figures 2–3 and Tables 3–7.

M1.justification: The Kalman-filter client models, linear augmentation, losses, gradient updates and communications remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. Corrections to the analytical recurrence concern its mathematical representation rather than a revised training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic mean-shift systems, causality perturbations, network topologies and HAI/SWaT datasets. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains the same three comparators: no client augmentation, no server model and pre-trained client. The centralized-oracle comparisons and Appendix A.8 baseline discussion also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The experimental settings, scalability configurations, metrics and testing procedures are unchanged. Section 9 retains the same Pearson-correlation threshold, SVD/VAR preprocessing and training on nominal data.

E4.justification: The component ablations, causality-perturbation and topology tests in Table 4, scalability analyses in Table 5 and supplementary baseline analysis in Appendix A.8 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Experimental uncertainty reporting and shaded loss plots are unchanged; no run counts, seed information or statistical procedures are added. Expectations introduced in the revised proofs are mathematical changes, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results and empirical findings match throughout. For example, Table 7 retains HAI/SWaT estimation errors of 0.8140/3.0816 and communication savings of 144/176 bytes per round.

T1.justification: Proposition 5.3 replaces a nonzero-Amm assumption and pointwise identities with full-rank/nonzero-measurement assumptions and expectation-based conditions. Theorem 6.1 replaces convergence of expected error norm with the substantially weaker convergence of mean error and requires full-rank Cmm. Theorem 5.4 adds a Kronecker identity factor to Pmm and corrects the residual time index in D. Corresponding appendix proofs, Definition A.3 and the dependencies of the Proposition 6.2 bound are revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, research objective, five stated contributions and conclusion retain the same headline claims. The formal weakening of oracle convergence in Theorem 6.1 is not accompanied by a revision of those contribution statements.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4.3 newly interprets the revised client condition as unbiased reconstruction of expected measurements, replacing the previous pointwise residual treatment. The empirical interpretations, Appendix A.7 summaries and Appendix A.9 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access information, pseudocode, model-function descriptions and preprocessing details are unchanged. No implementation settings, hardware information or resource disclosures are added.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are unchanged, including the positioning relative to vertical federated learning, system identification and distributed Kalman filtering.

P1.justification: Localized proof prose is expanded and rewritten, particularly in Appendices A.4.3 and A.4.8, with small punctuation and cross-reference updates. The overall narrative and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded proofs change equation spacing and page breaks, shifting existing appendix material across pages 20–27. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–7 retain their designs and placements.

improvement.justification: V4 usefully narrows Theorem 6.1 and corrects the Kronecker factor and residual index in Theorem 5.4. However, the rewritten Proposition 5.3 introduces incompatible scalar/matrix dimensions in Equation 29 for vector states, while Equations 25–26 unjustifiably infer zero mean residual from zero expected gradient. These proof problems coexist with clearer qualifications, and the empirical evidence is unchanged, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
